title: Breast Augmentation Scars: Where They Are, How They Fade
meta_description: Scars sit in the breast crease, at the areola edge or in the armpit. They fade over months to a couple of years but never vanish. Florida sun rules too.
excerpt: Breast augmentation scars sit in one of three places and fade over several months to a couple of years, but they never completely disappear. Here is what each incision means, what the evidence says about scar care, and how to protect new scars in the Florida sun.
quick_answer:
Do breast augmentation scars go away?

They fade but never fully disappear. ASPS says incision lines may take several months, even a couple of years, to fade, and Cleveland Clinic says a scar never completely goes away. Scars usually sit in the crease under the breast, at the edge of the areola or in the armpit.

images.text_in_image:
Scar Care: What the Evidence Says
Sun protection: SPF 30 or higher, or cover up. Sun can darken new scars.
Silicone sheets or gel: weak evidence for abnormal scars (Cochrane review, 20 trials, 873 people). Worth asking about.
Scar massage: common advice, no set schedule. Ask your surgeon.
Not smoking: nicotine affects scar quality.
Sources: MedlinePlus, Cochrane, ASPS

images.alt: Card titled New Scar: Normal, or See Your Surgeon? Usually normal: pink or red at first, or dark spots on darker skin, slight swelling for a while, sometimes itchy, tape or glue coming off on its own. See your surgeon: pus or bad-smelling drainage, stitches that open, spreading redness or heat, a scar growing thick, raised or spreading. Sources: Cleveland Clinic, UW Medicine and an article on the ASPS website.
